articles.title: Volunteers Turn Out for the Fall Cleanup Across Bellwood
articles.deck: Residents of Bellwood filled the hall on Saturday to ask questions about the plan.
body: The plan calls for pet adoption fair along Sawmill Avenue, with work expected to start in August.
The Bellwood Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library. Public works estimates the work will take about 27 weeks once it begins.
The group has raised $850 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. Talia Abernathy, who has lived in Bellwood for 27 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

articles.title: Eastgate Gets $3,400 for Second Recycling Drop-off
articles.deck: The money will be spent over the next year, with the first work starting in August.
body: The group has raised $3,400 so far and is asking for help with supplies and food. The plan calls for second recycling drop-off along Maple Road, with work expected to start in August.
Public works estimates the work will take about 33 weeks once it begins.

articles.title: Budget Hearing Draws 31 Residents
articles.deck: Supporters and opponents on Union Road disagreed about cost and timing.
body: Staff recommended approval with two conditions: a traffic study and a public notice period of 30 days.
Public works estimates the work will take about 31 weeks once it starts in September.
Residents of Canal Park said they had been asking for action for years, and several brought photographs of the street.

articles.title: Angela Beaudry, 94, Mail Carrier
articles.deck: Friends remember Angela Beaudry for the many years of service to Canal Park.
body: Angela Beaudry died in July at home on Coal Terrace, at the age of 94. Services will be held at the parish hall, and donations may be made to Scout Troop 14 in his or her name.

Survivors include a daughter, two grandchildren and many friends from Canal Park. Born in Canal Park in the years after the war, Angela Beaudry spent most of a working life in the trades and most of a retirement in the neighborhood.

articles.title: Letters: Salem Drive Parking Is Out of Control
body: To the editor: I have lived on Salem Drive for 27 years, and I want to say what a difference the Bellwood Chapel has made.
I hope the council will listen to the people who turned out at the August meeting.
Eleanor Szabo, Lower Millrace

articles.title: Then & Now: Birch Terrace in 1988 and Today
articles.deck: A photo from the Millrace County Historical Society shows the same corner as it looked decades ago.
body: A 1988 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Birch Terrace from the corner of Cooper Drive. Someone took the same picture from the same spot this month, holding the camera at about the same height.

Most of the houses are still standing, though the porches and the trees have changed a good deal. A 1988 photograph from the Millrace County Historical Society shows Birch Terrace from the corner of Cooper Drive.

articles.title: Marsh Landing Garden Club Adds Playground Upgrade
articles.deck: The work is expected to take 20 weeks and will be paid for with $18,500 raised locally.
body: Anyone interested can attend the next planning meeting at the Foundry Row fire house on Monday at 7 p.m. The Marsh Landing Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library.
Organizers say the work is on schedule and that volunteers are still needed on Monday mornings.
The effort began in February when a handful of neighbors met at the Foundry Row fire house to talk about playground upgrade.

body: The Eastgate Improvement Group will post updates on its bulletin board outside the library. Simone Renner, who has lived on Willow Street for 37 years, said the response has been better than anyone expected.

articles.title: Foxglove Heights Elementary Adds Free Tax Clinic to Fall Schedule
articles.deck: Principal Roman Corrigan said the school is grateful to families who volunteered this year.
body: Students will meet on Saturday afternoons in St. Brendan’s hall, and transportation will be provided for those who need it.

The board will review the results at the end of the fall term.
